title: How the thyroid regulates metabolism
intro: The thyroid lies at the front of the neck and releases hormones that influence energy use, temperature and many body functions. Symptoms of imbalance overlap with other illnesses; weight or tiredness alone is not a thyroid diagnosis.

sections.heading: Making hormones
paragraphs: Thyroid follicles use iodine to make and store thyroid hormones. The body obtains iodine from food, but more iodine is not always better; excess can also disturb thyroid function.

sections.heading: Feedback control
paragraphs: Pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone helps regulate output. Thyroid hormone levels feed back to the pituitary. Results need interpretation together and with pregnancy, medicines and possible pituitary disease in mind.

sections.heading: Too little or too much
paragraphs: Low output can slow functions; excess can cause heat intolerance, tremor or palpitations. Symptoms vary and develop at different speeds; a neck swelling does not by itself show hormone output.

sections.heading: Tests and treatment
paragraphs: Blood tests assess function; ultrasound assesses structure when indicated. Treatment depends on the cause. Do not adjust thyroid medicines from weight changes alone or use thyroid hormone for unprescribed weight loss.

sections.heading: Follow-up and safety
paragraphs: Tell the team about pregnancy plans, supplements and other medicines, and attend agreed blood tests. Severe palpitations with chest pain, breathlessness, high fever or marked confusion requires urgent assessment.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.
